lines: The app ships no composer/autoload.php, so the server registers its generic loader for lib/ and looks every class up in the file system.

A composer/composer.json with config.vendor-dir ".", config.optimize-autoloader true, a config.autoloader-suffix and autoload.psr-4 {"OCA\\OcrSearch\\": "../lib/"} makes composer dump-autoload write composer/autoload.php with a class map; the code of the app does not change.

places: lib/Service/Settings.php:70 OCP\IAppConfig::deleteKey(): deprecated since Nextcloud 13; use method deleteAppValue of \OCP\IConfig
lines: 1 use in 1 file of the public API that is deprecated in Nextcloud 33 to 35. The text of the tag names the replacement where it has one.
lib/Service/Settings.php:70 OCP\IAppConfig::deleteKey(): deprecated since Nextcloud 13; use method deleteAppValue of \OCP\IConfig

3 inline styles in templates/. The default Content Security Policy of the server allows inline style; a response whose policy disallows it drops them. A stylesheet added with OCP\Util::addStyle() holds in both cases.

1 timed job does not say whether it is time sensitive. A job that sets TIME_INSENSITIVE with setTimeSensitivity() is moved to the maintenance window of the server; whether a job is heavy enough for that only its maintainer knows.
lib/ reads the clock directly in 7 places. OCP\AppFramework\Utility\ITimeFactory, a PSR-20 ClockInterface, gives the same time and can be replaced in a test.

The app reads and writes its app config in 7 places and registers no config lexicon, which IRegistrationContext::registerConfigLexicon() takes since Nextcloud 31. A lexicon states the type, the default and the sensitivity of each key in one place.
